standard_prerequisites.name: The unramified locus is compatible with base change
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equality of the two unramified point sets.

standard_prerequisites.name: A morphism is etale at a point exactly when it is flat and unramified there
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the unramified statement into the etale statement in case (1).

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness is preserved by base change and by composition, and is detected at the source point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-base-change-module-flat}, Lemma \ref{lemma-composition-module-flat} and Lemma \ref{lemma-flat-permanence}, cited at proof lines 8447-8453

standard_prerequisites.name: The etale-at-a-point criterion
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the morphism is etale at the image point in case (2).

core_obligations: Reduce to the unramified locus, which is compatible with base change (proof lines 8434-8440).
Case (1): identify the etale locus with the unramified locus using flat plus unramified (proof lines 8442-8445).
Case (2): transport flatness along the square and the composition and apply the etale-at-a-point criterion (proof lines 8446-8456).
proof_roadmap: Case (1) via flat plus unramified (proof lines 8442-8445).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a cartesian square of schemes the open set of points where the top morphism is etale is the preimage of the corresponding open set for the bottom morphism, provided either that morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, or it is locally of finite presentation and the base change morphism is flat. The proof reduces to the unramified locus, which is already known to be compatible with arbitrary base change, and then splits into the two cases: in the first the etale locus equals the unramified locus by flatness plus unramifiedness, and in the second flatness of the relevant morphisms is transported along the square and the composition, so that flatness at the image point follows and the etale-at-a-point criterion concludes.
